Article Title: Peter Thiel to all billionaires and others blaming China for anti-AI backlash in America: Stop doing this, you cannot ...
Article Text:
Peter Thiel

Peter Thiel says US is largely responsible for AI backlash

AI debate increasingly linked to US-China rivalry

Peter Thiel has pushed back against claims that China is behind growing anti-AI sentiment in the US, saying Americans should look at their own actions instead. In an interview with Axel Springer CEO Mathias Döpfner on the “MD Meets” podcast recently, the PayPal co-founder said he is “inclined to believe” China could be fueling some anti-AI content, but does not see it as the main reason for the change in public sentiment. “This is mainly what we’re doing to ourselves,” Thiel said. “It’s often somewhat too easy to simply blame it on China.”Peter Thiel's comments come as some US technology executives have blamed China, America's main AI rival, for growing criticism of the technology. Thiel, who has himself been a strong critic of China, said the country should be taken seriously but argued against blaming it for every development around AI.Asked whether China was promoting anti-AI material on American social media, Thiel said he had not studied the issue closely. He said he was inclined to believe it was happening, but added that it was not the main factor behind the backlash.Thiel also criticised Pope Leo XIV's May 2026 AI encyclical, describing it as anti-AI. He argued that the Chinese Communist Party would not listen to the Pope, while people in the US might.“I'm not saying he was an agent of the communists,” Thiel said, “but he was at least acting as a useful idiot for the CCP.”Thiel later said he may have put the point too strongly, but repeated his argument that the Pope's message could have an effect in the US while China would not follow it.Thiel’s comments come as AI development has become closely tied to competition between the US and China. The US has accused Chinese AI companies of copying American AI technology, while China has rejected those claims.At the same time, concerns about AI's impact on jobs, safety, security and society have grown in the US. Thiel's argument is that those concerns should not automatically be attributed to Chinese influence. In the “MD Meets” interview, he said the US should instead examine how its own decisions and discussions are shaping public attitudes toward AI.
Article Summary: Peter Thiel says US is largely responsible for AI backlash. PayPal co-founder says he is 'inclined to believe' China could be fueling some anti-AI content. Thiel also criticised Pope Leo XIV's May 2026 AI encyclical as 'anti-AI'

Article Title: A power bank sold online for as little as $27 is being recalled after nine reports of units exploding or catching fire; one incident caused a serious blaze with an estimated $2 million in property dam
Article Text:
Image: US Consumer Product Safety Commission

Which power banks are being recalled after nine reports of units exploding

Nine reports included explosions and fires

The power banks were sold on Amazon for $27 to $50

Consumers have been told to stop using the device

What consumers should check before seeking a refund

A NEWDERY power bank sold online for as little as $27 has been recalled in the US after nine reports of the devices exploding and catching fire, according to the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). One of the incidents involved a serious fire that caused an estimated $2 million in property damage, while another resulted in a burn injury. The recall, announced on September 24, 2026, affects about 21,380 power banks with model number ZHX-PB22. The lithium-ion batteries inside the devices can explode or ignite, creating fire and burn hazards. The affected products were sold on Amazon.com between October 2023 and November 2024 for between $27 and $50.The recall covers NEWDERY power banks with the model number ZHX-PB22. The affected units are black and come with yellow cables. The NEWDERY brand name is engraved on the front, while the model number is printed on the back of the device. The products were manufactured in China and imported by Shenzhen Xinkewangda Electronics Co., Ltd., doing business as NEWDERY. According to the CPSC, about 21,380 units are covered by the September 2026 recall.The recalled power bank is a portable device containing a lithium-ion battery. The CPSC says the battery can explode or ignite, presenting fire and burn hazards to consumers. Consumers who have one of the affected devices can check the model number on the back of the power bank. They should not rely only on the appearance of the device, as the specific model number, ZHX-PB22, is the key identifier given in the recall notice.The recall follows nine reports received by NEWDERY involving the recalled power banks exploding and igniting.One of those reports involved a serious fire that caused approximately $2 million in property damage, according to the CPSC. Another report involved a burn injury. The CPSC has not provided further details in its recall notice about the location of the $2 million fire, what property was damaged or how the incident unfolded. Those details should therefore not be inferred beyond the agency's description. The agency identifies the lithium-ion battery as the source of the hazard. Lithium-ion batteries can store substantial amounts of energy, and failures can result in overheating, fire or other dangerous events. In this case, the CPSC specifically warns that the battery in the recalled NEWDERY power banks can explode or ignite.The affected power banks were sold through Amazon.com from October 2023 to November 2024, according to the latest CPSC recall notice. Their reported selling price ranged from $27 to $50. That means the $27 figure refers to the lowest reported selling price for the recalled product, rather than the price of the particular power bank involved in the $2 million property-damage incident. The September 2026 recall covers about 21,380 units. The products were manufactured in China and imported by Shenzhen Xinkewangda Electronics Co., Ltd., which operates under the NEWDERY name. There is also an important history behind the recall. In June 2025, the CPSC had already warned consumers to immediately stop using NEWDERY ZHX-PB22 power banks after receiving the same nine reports of explosions and fires. At that time, the agency said about 17,670 defective units had been sold exclusively on Amazon from March 2023 through November 2024 for $27 to $50. The 2025 notice said the importer had refused to conduct a recall. The figures from the two notices should not be combined. The 17,670-unit figure belongs to the June 2025 warning, while the 21,380-unit figure belongs to the September 2026 recall.The CPSC is now telling consumers to stop using the recalled power banks immediately and contact NEWDERY for instructions on obtaining a full refund. Consumers seeking a refund will have to provide a photograph of the recalled power bank showing its model number and serial number, along with the word ‘recalled’ and the consumer's last name written on the device in permanent marker. They will also have to confirm that the power bank has been disposed of in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The disposal instructions are particularly important because the CPSC says recalled lithium-ion batteries should not be placed in ordinary household rubbish or general recycling.Consumers are also advised not to put the device into street-level or curbside recycling bins or used battery recycling boxes commonly found at retail and home-improvement stores. Instead, they should contact their local household hazardous waste collection centre to ask whether it accepts recalled lithium-ion batteries. If it does not, the CPSC advises consumers to contact their municipality for further guidance.Anyone who owns a NEWDERY power bank should first check whether it matches the recalled model. The key identifier is ZHX-PB22, printed on the back. The recalled units are black and have yellow cables, with the NEWDERY name on the front. The CPSC lists NEWDERY's consumer contact number as 888-256-6673, available from 11am to 7pm ET Monday through Friday. Consumers can also contact the company by email at support@newdery.com or use the recall information provided on NEWDERY's website. The September 24 recall carries CPSC recall number 26-792. For consumers, the central message is straightforward, if the power bank is the recalled ZHX-PB22 model, it should no longer be used, and it should be handled through the recall and appropriate hazardous-waste disposal process rather than being thrown into ordinary rubbish or recycling.
Article Summary: The recall covers NEWDERY power banks with the model number ZHX-PB22. The lithium-ion batteries inside the devices can explode or ignite, creating fire and burn hazards. One of the incidents involved a serious fire that caused an estimated $2 million in property damage, while another resulted in a burn injury. The affected products were sold on Amazon.com between October 2023 and November 2024 for between $27 and $50.

Article Title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber is its fourth cybersecurity model this year, here's what's coming
Article Text:
OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber: Timing amid growing AI security concerns

Part of a bigger DevDay push

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI is preparing to unveil its latest cybersecurity-focused model named GPT-6 Cyber. According to a report by Fortune, OpenAI will introduce the new model in the coming weeks. The report claims that the model will be designed to help customers deploy the model more securely and automate workflows to patch vulnerabilities. The launch comes as governments and enterprises grapple with increasingly sophisticated AI‑powered cyberattacks. The yet‑to‑be‑named product will function as a gateway, similar to how ChatGPT serves as the entry point for consumer models like GPT‑6 Astra. It will allow enterprises to build automated defenses while giving OpenAI greater oversight into how its models are used. A limited number of customers in OpenAI’s Daybreak Red program — the company’s advanced cybersecurity access tier — are already testing GPT‑6 Cyber in alpha.The upcoming release lands at an awkward moment for OpenAI's public image on security. The company, along with other major AI labs, has faced intense scrutiny recently following a string of incidents in which "rogue" AI agents broke out of their intended sandboxes and accessed outside systems, including breaches at Hugging Face and an Australian government website.Still, the launch of GPT-6 Cyber isn't a reaction to those incidents — it's part of a cybersecurity product line OpenAI has been steadily building out over the course of the year.GPT-6 Cyber will be the fourth cybersecurity-focused model OpenAI has released in 2026 alone, following GPT-5.4 Cyber in April, GPT-5.5 Cyber in June, and GPT-5.6 Cyber in August. The company has been ramping up enterprise sales specifically around these cybersecurity tools, an effort now led by Chief Revenue Officer Dali Rajic, who joined OpenAI in August. Earlier this month, OpenAI also pledged $1 billion to subsidize the use of its cybersecurity products for organizations providing critical services.GPT-6 Cyber's unveiling is expected to be just one piece of a much larger product rollout at OpenAI's annual DevDay event on September 29, where the company reportedly plans to ship a dozen or more products spanning both enterprise and consumer offerings, most unrelated to cybersecurity. According to a source familiar with the plans, OpenAI has deliberately held off on any major launches over the past two weeks — aside from its affordability-focused GPT-6 Sol and Luna models — specifically to save them for a concentrated release at DevDay. CEO Sam Altman had already teased the scale of what's coming earlier this month, posting a string of ship emojis on X to hint at the lineup ahead.
Article Summary: GPT-6 Cyber will be the fourth cybersecurity-focused model OpenAI has released in 2026. It will allow enterprises to build automated defenses while giving OpenAI greater oversight into how its models are used. The launch comes as governments and enterprises grapple with increasingly sophisticated AI‑powered cyberattacks.

Article Title: Oracle market value loses millions; as notice sent on data center project in New Mexico 'surfaces', company told developer Blue Owl Capital that …
Article Text:
Oracle

What is Force Majeure and understanding Oracle’s move

The Stargate anchor and debt

Oracle is taking legal steps to protect itself from accumulating expenses on a massive artificial intelligence (AI) data center in southern New Mexico, marking a sharp escalation for an infrastructure project mired in public opposition and regulatory hurdles. Citing individuals familiar with the matter, a report by Bloomberg says that the enterprise technology giant has sent a formal notice citing force majeure to the project’s developer, a unit of alternative asset manager Blue Owl Capital. Following this development, Oracle’s shares fell 4%, losing millions of dollars from its market cap.The report notes that rather than walking away entirely as the anchor tenant, Oracle is seeking to defer contractual payments if the facility, internally named Project Jupiter, encounters further delays and misses its planned 2028 operational target.Companies generally invoke force majeure to suspend or excuse contractual duties when uncontrollable events prevent performance. In this dispute, Oracle is asserting its contractual standing ahead of potential construction bottlenecks. However, it remains uncertain whether the maneuver will legally relieve Oracle of its earlier financial obligations.Addressing the situation publicly, an Oracle spokesperson affirmed the facility's target delivery, saying, “Project Jupiter remains on our planned schedule.We are fully committed to New Mexico and confident in our path forward.”The southern New Mexico facility was planned as a cornerstone of the broader Stargate AI infrastructure push. US President Donald Trump originally unveiled the venture alongside top executives from Oracle, OpenAI, and SoftBank Group, framing it during the early days of his second term as a historic investment unseen in modern tech history.Nearly two years later, the campus reportedly faces steep challenges. One of them is the massive energy scale. The hub was engineered to draw 2.45 gigawatts, which is equivalent to the steady electricity demand of roughly 1.8 million homes. The second is financing pressure as a syndicate of approximately 20 commercial banks backed the campus with an $18 billion construction loan, representing one of the largest debt packages financing the generative AI boom.Thirdly, even if deployed purely as a legal safeguard, Oracle's notice risks unnerving institutional debt holders. The debt backing the project is already trading at distressed levels below 90 cents on the dollar.The disclosure also highlights contractual vulnerabilities in hyperscale leases, where tech firms commonly reserve termination rights if developers miss committed handover dates. An earlier example occurred when Alphabet's Google contracted with Elon Musk's SpaceX for computing power through mid-2029 while retaining rights to exit if capacity failed to materialize on schedule.
Article Summary: Oracle is taking legal steps to protect itself from accumulating expenses on a massive artificial intelligence (AI) data center in southern New Mexico. Oracle is seeking to defer contractual payments if the facility, internally named Project Jupiter, encounters further delays and misses its planned 2028 operational target. It remains uncertain whether the maneuver will legally relieve Oracle of earlier financial obligations.

Article Text: YouTube Shopping is set to expand its merchant ecosystem in India with the addition of Amazon, AJIO, Meesho, Snapdeal and Tata CLiQ, while new AI-powered tools are expected to make product discovery and creator monetisation more seamless ahead of the festive shopping season. YouTube on Thursday announced the expansion of its YouTube Shopping affiliate programme in India, adding the new partners to existing retailers including Flipkart, Myntra, Nykaa, Purplle, Shopsy and Tira. The company said the expansion will give consumers and creators access to a wider range of products across value marketplaces, major retailers and specialised beauty brands.The move comes as creator earnings through YouTube Shopping continue to rise. Average payouts to Indian creators grew more than 160 per cent year-on-year between the first quarters of 2025 and 2026, compared with more than 100 per cent growth globally.More than 50 per cent of eligible Indian creators are now enrolled in the programme, with enrolment growing 200 per cent year-on-year. These creators have tagged more than 19 million videos, according to the company.YouTube said more than 450 million logged-in users in India search for shopping-related content on the platform, while shopping-related watch time in the country has increased 55 per cent year-on-year.Alongside the merchant expansion, YouTube is introducing new AI tools for viewers, creators and brands. Its Ask YouTube for Shopping feature will allow viewers to ask questions and follow up on products directly on a video's watch page, including through voice commands while watching on TV.YouTube is also updating product tags for creators with global audiences, with tagged products adapting to domestic deals from regional retailers and local currencies based on the viewer's location. The company said this will allow Indian creators to earn commissions more seamlessly from international audiences.The platform is further expanding tools that allow brands to amplify organic creator affiliate content through paid campaigns. Ask Studio for Brand Partnerships, which is rolling out soon, will use generative AI to help creators pitch campaigns and respond to brand briefs.Exclusive Affiliate Campaigns, offering bonus incentives and higher commission rates, are scheduled to roll out in India next year. Globally, shopping-related watch time on YouTube crossed 40 billion hours in 2025, while gross merchandise value grew 13-fold over two years.
Article Summary: YouTube is set to expand its merchant ecosystem in India with the addition of Amazon, AJIO, Meesho, Snapdeal and Tata CLiQ. New AI-powered tools are expected to make product discovery and creator monetisation more seamless ahead of the festive shopping season.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Bill Gates: 'I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act'
Article Text:
“I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act.”

Quote of the day

“I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act.” Bill Gates

What the quote actually means

Who is the customer

What are their needs and priorities

What's happening in the market

What are competitors doing

What are our options for responding

How do we differentiate

How is technology changing and what possibilities does it offer customers

What are the business priorities

Why this mindset is more important than it seems

“Here is what is wrong,”

“Here is what is wrong, here is why it matters and here are the ways we could address it.”

We all come across problems that can feel too complicated, distant or difficult to solve. Whether it is a challenge at work, a business problem, or a larger issue affecting society, simply pointing out that something is wrong doesn't always lead to action. People are more likely to respond when they understand both the problem and what can be done about it.That's the idea behind a quote by Bill Gates, the entrepreneur and philanthropist, who said:The thought highlights the importance of presenting a problem with enough context to help people understand it, while also showing them a possible path forward.Gates' statement is closely connected to framing a problem. A problem can look very different depending on how it is presented, just like a picture can look different depending on how it is framed.Framing a problem means deciding what needs attention, what information matters, and what perspective can help people understand the challenge more clearly. It also puts boundaries around the problem, making it easier to examine rather than treating it as one large, undefined issue.But framing is not only about identifying what is wrong. It is also about putting the problem into context and showing people their options.For example, instead of simply saying a business is losing customers, a better approach is to look at who those customers are, what they need, what is changing in the market, and what competitors are doing differently.Some questions that can help frame a problem include:Understanding who is affected by the problem can help define what needs to be addressed.Knowing what matters to the people affected can make the problem more specific and easier to solve.A problem may be connected to broader changes that need to be considered before deciding on a response.Looking at how others approach a similar challenge can offer another perspective on the problem.Identifying possible solutions shifts the discussion from describing a problem to considering what we can do about it.Understanding what makes an approach different can help determine how to present or implement a solution.Technology can change both the nature of a problem and the solutions available to address it.A solution also needs to fit within the organisation's broader priorities.It is easy to tell people that something needs to change. It is much harder to get them to understand why it matters and what they can actually do about it.That is where framing becomes important. A problem presented without context can feel overwhelming or irrelevant. But when people can see the problem clearly and understand the possible solutions, they have a better basis for deciding how to respond.The same approach can apply to everyday challenges. At work, for example, saying that a project is falling behind may not be enough to get people moving. Explaining what is causing the delay, who is affected and what options are available gives the team a clearer picture of the situation.The idea also changes the way we communicate problems. Instead of stopping atthe conversation becomesThat shift can make a problem easier to understand and give people a clearer reason to act.
Article Summary: Bill Gates said: “I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act.” Framing a problem means deciding what needs attention, what information matters, and what perspective can help people understand the challenge more clearly.

Article Title: Inside Amazon India’s playbook for the Great Indian Festival 2026
Article Text:
Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India

In a conversation with The Times of India, Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at

Amazon India

"To make our delivery experience more integrated and seamless, we have our Unified Delivery Service across over 300 cities, alongside, we have recently introduced Open Box Delivery on eligible high-value products will allow customers to verify the product at the time of delivery before accepting it. Together, these offerings bring greater choice, value, discovery and convenience to customers this festive season." Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India

‘Rising component costs has not dented premium ambitions’

‘AI popularity moves beyond smartphones’

Amazon Great India Festival dates

India’s consumer electronics landscape is seemingly seeing a decisive shift. The days of impulsive gadget buying and settling for bare-minimum entry-level devices are giving way to deliberate, research-intensive decisions. As households gear up for the festive season, shoppers are demanding premium hardware, tangible artificial intelligence capabilities, and transparent value., spoke about the emerging trends driving tech adoption across the country, drawing insights from the platform’s 'Best in Tech' Survey."As customers become more deliberate and research-led in their technology purchases, the Best in Tech Survey was conducted to understand the features, innovations and value propositions that matter most to them across categories," Khan explained. The survey, based on 40,000-plus responses across primary consumer electronics categories, revealed that consumer priorities have fractured into distinct, highly specialized buckets.In the smartphone arena, the baseline expectations, as per Amazon survey, remain rooted in speed and battery stamina, with raw performance leading the pack. Yet, emerging software capabilities are swiftly ascending the priority list.A striking 82% of survey respondents noted they expect integrated AI features in their next phone, with nearly half intending to upgrade within three months.A parallel evolution is taking place in personal computing. Processor performance remains paramount—cited by 87% of laptop buyers as their primary driver—while 58% view upcoming AI tools as indispensable for productivity. Users are seeking dedicated on-device AI assistants, neural-processing silicon, and built-in creation tools rather than generic hardware refreshes. Meanwhile, tablets have transitioned into visual-first media and work hubs: 74% of buyers prioritize screen size and panel quality over price, with the Rs 20,000–Rs 35,000 sweet spot capturing 59% of total consideration.The electronics industry has weathered consecutive waves of inflationary pressure driven by surging memory and chipset costs. Yet, rather than trading down to cheaper alternatives, Indian consumers are exercising patience. "There is no doubt that prices are rising and customers have seen several rounds of pricing increases due to higher chip and memory costs. At the same time, we are seeing a lot of pent-up demand, with customers holding on to their upgrades rather than compromising on what they want. Premiumisation is not going away," said Khan.According to Khan, rather than sacrificing build quality or performance, consumers are bridging the affordability gap through structured financing mechanisms. Exchange schemes, bank tie-ups, instant credit via Amazon Pay, and No-Cost EMI plans have evolved into essential purchasing levers. For large appliances, 47% of consumers identify No-Cost EMI as their single most critical pricing enabler."Customers continue to look for premium smartphones, laptops and appliances and are willing to invest in better features, performance and experiences when they see the right combination of value and affordability," Khan emphasized.While artificial intelligence dominates tech headlines, Khan highlighted that consumers are discerning when it comes to practical utility. The buzz around generative tools has evolved into a demand for meaningful everyday workflows. "We are seeing growing interest in AI across categories. Customers are increasingly drawn to products with AI features as they discover and understand what the technology can do, but the final decision continues to come down to genuine performance and the value they are getting," she said.Importantly, Khan noted that beyond smartphones, interest in AI extends to laptops, where AI capabilities are increasingly becoming part of the upgrade cycle; and to categories such as TVs and smart home appliances, where AI-enabled features are becoming part of the consideration. The broader trend is towards customers looking for technology that is relevant to their specific use cases, whether that is gaming, creation, work or everyday use. She said, "It definitely extends beyond smartphones. On smartphones, AI features are becoming increasingly important as customers discover and understand what the technology can do, but they continue to evaluate the device on fundamentals such as camera, processing speed and everyday performance. Beyond smartphones, we are seeing this interest extend to laptops... and to categories such as TVs and smart home appliances."Giving more example she added that from energy-smart inverter refrigerators to AI-enhanced upscaling in smart televisions, buyers are evaluating machines through the lens of longevity and personal utility.To meet increase in demand as it heads into the Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026, the e-commerce giant is overhauling both discovery and post-purchase fulfillment. AI tools such as the conversational shopping assistant Rufus, visual search via LensAI, curated Smartchoice selection, and automated review summaries aim to cut through cluttered spec sheets."This festive season, we are focused on making product discovery easier and helping customers make more confident decisions," Khan noted, pointing out that peace of mind extends all the way to the doorstep. "Customers can benefit from open-box delivery on eligible products, giving them the opportunity to verify the product at the time of delivery. Our installation services are available across over 300 cities, helping customers get their appliances set up conveniently after purchase. "Amazon Great Indian Festival starts on October 8, 2026. According to online giant, there will be deals across all popular categories, including smartphones, electronics, fashion, beauty, home essentials and grocery. Customers also get a 10% instant discount on SBI Credit and Debit Cards and EMI transactions, and up to 10% extra only for Prime members.
Article Summary: Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India, spoke about the emerging trends driving tech adoption across the country. The days of impulsive gadget buying and settling for bare-minimum entry-level devices are giving way to deliberate, research-intensive decisions.

93% of Indian auto buyers turn to AI experiences for research; finds Google study

Key findings from the study

Google has released a study on the “Automobile Purchase Journey in the Age of AI”, highlighting how AI and digital surfaces are reshaping how India buys cars. According to the study, 93% of shoppers actively turn to AI during their research phase. Within this landscape, Google Search AI experiences play a critical role in evaluating complex specifications and financing. Consumers using AI actively navigate an average of 7.8 touchpoints to research and validate choices, reflecting a deeply considered, non-linear purchase journey, the study says.The study reveals that 87% of car buyers engage with Google platforms—including Search, YouTube, Maps, and Gemini—with Google Search widely cited by respondents as a key destination in the active research phase.Commenting on the evolving consumer journey, Siddharth Shekhar, Director, Google India, said, “The car buying journey in India is deliberate, non-linear, and deeply digital—particularly ahead of the festive season, when consideration peaks. Buyers move between discovery on YouTube and conversational validation on Search. Among surveyed Google Search users, 90% come across AI Overviews and 89% AI chatbots’ refers to conversational AI assistants such as Gemini and others.‘AI surfaces’ is a broader term encompassing these conversational assistants as well as generative AI experiences in Google Search that is AI Overviews and AI Mode. use AI Mode to navigate nuanced, complex queries. As AI helps buyers navigate complex choices, our ad and commerce solutions help automotive brands respond to their intent—connecting initial curiosity directly to the showroom.”Indian car buyers view their vehicle as a fundamental visual representation of personal achievement and lifestyle. However, final vehicle selection has decisively shifted toward a collaborative household effort, with 64% of consumers involving the whole family and 53% deciding alongside spouses.Among surveyed Google Search users, 90% come across AI Overviews and 89% leverage AI Mode for nuanced, conversational queries. Conversational AI triggers deeper validation: 80% of surveyed car buyers who use AI chatbots also turn to Google Search and/or YouTube during active research.YouTube functions as an always-on virtual showroom, where ~6 in 10 car buyers casually explore brands well ahead of their purchase decision. Through personalized Home Feeds, lifestyle vlogs, and creator content, passive discovery evolves into active consideration, anchored by 77% of YouTube users who rely on professional reviewers for trusted advice.AI acts as an expansionary force in active researchVirat Khullar, Head – Marketing, Hyundai Motor India Limited said,"The automotive purchase journey is increasingly shaped by moments of discovery, research and intent across digital channels. Our partnership with Google helped us harness the scale of YouTube to build awareness and the intelligence of AI-powered Search ad solutions to identify and convert high-intent consumers. By unifying upper- and lower-funnel marketing, we were able to deliver a more relevant and efficient customer experience, turning consideration into action and driving strong sales momentum for Hyundai VERNA. "

Article Title: Nike cofounder Phil Knight makes largest known donation to public flagship university, made over an unscheduled call, University president calls the 'extraordinary gift an endorsement of ...'
Article Text:
Nike co-founder Phil Knight

Nike co-founder has given billions to Oregon causes

Phil Knight’s donation comes as US university funding faces uncertainty

Nike cofounder Phil Knight just made the largest known donation to a public flagship university in the US. According to a New York Times report, Phil Knight and his wife Penny have donated a whopping $1 billion to the University of Oregon. The donation, surfaced from an unscheduled call, will go toward establishing an engineering college in the University. The latest pledge adds to previous donations by the Knights. Last week, they committed $1.1 billion to Providence St. Vincent Medical Center and Providence Heart Institute in Portland. In 2025, they gave $2 billion to OHSU’s Knight Cancer Institute. Knight, 88, has a net worth of nearly $23 billion, according to Bloomberg.Responding to the donation, Karl Scholz, president of the University of Oregon, told Fortune: “This extraordinary gift is an endorsement of what higher education delivers. It gives us the ability to scale innovation, accelerate impact, and meet the demand for skilled engineering required by the industries of tomorrow, all without placing that financial burden on state taxpayers.”The couple has also made major donations linked to University of Oregon athletics.They have previously given $100 million to build the university’s basketball arena, named in honour of their late son, Matthew Knight.Phil Knight’s support has also helped create strong ties between the university and Nike. Oregon athletes have access to new and exclusive Nike gear, along with support related to name, image and likeness (NIL) deals. Because of the close relationship, some people call Oregon the “University of Nike.”Phil Knights’ donation comes as federal support for universities faces uncertainty. In early 2025, the Trump administration laid off thousands of workers at federal science agencies, delayed some grant payments to universities and sought cuts to funding for research overheads. The administration also withdrew some DEI grants.Additionally, the White House’s fiscal 2026 budget proposal called for a nearly 36% cut in non-defense science research and development funding. It also proposed cuts of nearly 57% at the National Science Foundation (NSF) and more than 40% at the National Institutes of Health (NIH). However, Congress largely rejected those proposed cuts and kept science funding mostly unchanged.
Article Summary: Phil Knight and his wife Penny have donated a whopping $1 billion to the University of Oregon. The donation, surfaced from an unscheduled call, will go toward establishing an engineering college in the University. Knight, 88, has a net worth of nearly $23 billion, according to Bloomberg.
